title: Securely passing access key to SparkOperator for Azure DataLake on K8s
question:
I'm having problems securely passing access key to a Spark Job using SparkOperator

I've got a KIND cluster running spark jobs using SparkOperator on an Azure Data Lake account using pyspark. Currently I'm programmatically sending manifests to the SparkOperator with hadoop configs hard coded to the manifest which is used to then call the pyspark scripts from the data lake. Something like this.

apiVersion: "sparkoperator.k8s.io/v1beta2"
kind: SparkApplication
metadata:
  name: spark-job
  namespace: spark-jobs
  ###lots of configs and jars###
  mainApplicationFile: "abfss://dwh@STORAGEACCOUNT.dfs.core.windows.net/test.py"
"spark.hadoop.fs.azure.account.auth.type.STORAGEACCOUNT.dfs.core.windows.net":"SharedKey"
"spark.hadoop.fs.azure.account.key.STORAGEACCOUNT.dfs.core.windows.net": "ACCESS_KEY"

This works perfectly, picks up the file from the lake and then writes back to the delta tables on ADLS2.

The problem is the ACCESS_KEY is plaintext which isn't really acceptable for anything beyond this POC. I've tried passing this as a Kubernetes secret in a number of methods based on the structure below

    "spark.kubernetes.driver.secrets.spark-secret": "/etc/secrets"
    "spark.kubernetes.executor.secrets.spark-secret": "/etc/secrets"
    "spark.kubernetes.driver.secretKeyRef.AZURE_KEY": "spark-secret:azure_storage_key"
    "spark.kubernetes.executor.secretKeyRef.AZURE_KEY": "spark-secret:azure_storage_key"
    #"spark.hadoop.fs.azure.account.key.STORAGEACCOUNT.dfs.core.windows.net": ${AZURE_KEY}

However this doesn't work. I've also tried similar secret methods trying to pickup the key as an ENV var in the extraJavaOptions conf:

spark.driver.extraJavaOptions,: "-Dfs.azure.account.key.STORAGEACCOUNT.dfs.core.windows.net=${AZURE_KEY}"

None of this works and I'm now out of ideas. Has anyone managed to do this securely or setup another authentication method on Azure that is secure enough for deploying in a production environment?
answer:
To securely pass the access key to a Spark job using SparkOperator, you can use Kubernetes secrets. Here is a step-by-step guide to achieve this:

First, create a Kubernetes secret to store your Azure storage account key.

kubectl create secret generic spark-secret --from-literal=azure_storage_key=YOUR_ACCESS_KEY

Update your SparkApplication manifest to mount the secret as an environment variable and use it in your Spark configuration.

apiVersion: "sparkoperator.k8s.io/v1beta2"
   kind: SparkApplication
   metadata:
     name: spark-job
     namespace: spark-jobs
   spec:
     type: Python
     pythonVersion: "3"
     mode: cluster
     image: "gcr.io/spark-operator/spark-py:v3.1.1"
     mainApplicationFile: "abfss://dwh@STORAGEACCOUNT.dfs.core.windows.net/test.py"
     sparkConf:
       "spark.hadoop.fs.azure.account.auth.type.STORAGEACCOUNT.dfs.core.windows.net": "SharedKey"
     driver:
       cores: 1
       memory: "512m"
       labels:
         version: 3.1.1
       serviceAccount: spark
       env:
         - name: AZURE_KEY
           valueFrom:
             secretKeyRef:
               name: spark-secret
               key: azure_storage_key
       envVars:
         - name: AZURE_KEY
           valueFrom:
             secretKeyRef:
               name: spark-secret
               key: azure_storage_key
     executor:
       cores: 1
       instances: 2
       memory: "512m"
       labels:
         version: 3.1.1
       env:
         - name: AZURE_KEY
           valueFrom:
             secretKeyRef:
               name: spark-secret
               key: azure_storage_key
       envVars:
         - name: AZURE_KEY
           valueFrom:
             secretKeyRef:
               name: spark-secret
               key: azure_storage_key
     sparkConfigMap: spark-config

Modify your Spark configuration to use the environment variable for the access key.

sparkConf:
     "spark.hadoop.fs.azure.account.auth.type.STORAGEACCOUNT.dfs.core.windows.net": "SharedKey"
     "spark.hadoop.fs.azure.account.key.STORAGEACCOUNT.dfs.core.windows.net": "${AZURE_KEY}"

In this way you can access key is securely stored in a Kubernetes secret and referenced in your Spark job without exposing it in plaintext.
